attributes.value: Niger is a branched annual herb belonging to Asteraceae family. It generally grows to a height of 1 to 2 meters, produces bright yellow flowers and black seeds which are rich in oil. Plants flower 45 to 60 days after sowing and mature in 90 to 110 days depending on the variety and season.

description.title: Whole genome sequencing of niger

assembly_info.comments: Niger Guizotia abyssinica L.f. Cass., belonging to the family Compositae Asteraceae, subtribe Coreopsidinae is a diploid 2n 2x 30 annual oilseed crop. The crop has its origin in Ethiopia and is cultivated in Asian countries like India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, and parts of China. In addition to the seed oil, various parts of the plant have several ethnomedicinal uses and are valued for their nutritional properties. The crop is quite hardy, grows on marginal lands and hilly tops and slopes and is less vulnerable to biotic and abiotic stresses as compared to other major annual oilseed crops. Varietal and hybrid development and trait improvement programmes are constrained by the strong self incompatibility and lack of genomic resources.
